title: Machine Catalog Convergence for Calculator + Shop Profiles
brief: Unify the 920-machine enriched corpus into a configuration-aware machine-package model that powers the calculator machine-selection module, preserves only legal controller/spindle/coolant/capability combinations, persists user-owned shop machine profiles for downstream reuse by Print to CNC, Program Release, quoting, what-if analysis, and other machine-aware consumers, and extends the calculator with PRISM mode recommendations that prefer owned inventory and rank missing-coverage purchases by price tier and ROI.

units.title: Inventory every machine source and every machine-consuming surface across calculator, registry, machine-profile, and program-release flows
Define the canonical machine taxonomy used by calculator modes and subfamilies
Define the machine-package schema covering controller, spindle, coolant, capabilities, provenance, and confidence
Generate the initial brand and machine-family gap matrix from the enriched corpus
Merge duplicate registry rows into configuration-aware machine packages instead of flat model records
Normalize manufacturer, model, controller, spindle, coolant, and capability vocabularies
Build per-machine allowed-option matrices so only legal controller, spindle, coolant, and package combinations survive
Add provenance, confidence, and unresolved-ambiguity queues for incomplete machine data
Replace residual heuristic-only filtering with package-driven filtering in the calculator machine-selection module
Surface controller capabilities, spindle packages, and coolant strategies directly from the machine-package truth model
Persist user-owned shop machine profiles and calculator machine presets as overlays on canonical machine packages
Add contract tests so unsupported options never render for the active machine package

phases.title: Downstream Machine-Profile Reuse + Calculator PRISM Mode

units.title: Bind Program Release and Print to CNC to the same canonical machine package plus user overlay used by the calculator
Expose machine-package read/write APIs and resource surfaces for other machine-aware products
Propagate machine-profile reuse into quoting, what-if analysis, scheduling, and feasibility consumers
Add calculator PRISM mode orchestration that derives best-fit tooling, holder, coolant, software, and toolpath categories from the active machine package, saved machine profile, and user inventory
Add ranked budget, standard, and premium acquisition recommendations with purchase-popup reuse, cutting-data confidence, compatibility, ROI, payback, and distributor evidence
Execute brand audit waves in priority order: Okuma, Haas, Mazak, Brother, Citizen, DN Solutions, and DMG MORI
Run calculator and downstream browser/system QA for machine-package selection and reuse
Add admin import/export and remediation flows for shop machine profiles
Publish machine-package coverage dashboards and the remaining ambiguity backlog

exit_conditions: The calculator machine-selection module resolves every supported machine through a canonical machine-package model rather than inconsistent raw rows
Controller, spindle, coolant, and capability options are filtered by published availability and impossible combinations do not render
User-owned shop machine profiles can be saved as overlays on canonical machine packages
Print to CNC and Program Release can consume the same machine package used by the calculator
The calculator can derive machine-legal, inventory-aware setup recommendations from the saved machine profile instead of forcing the user to hand-pick every category
Budget, standard, and premium purchase recommendations can be ranked by compatibility, cutting-data confidence, ROI, and payback without inventing unsupported combinations
Remaining brand or package ambiguities are explicit, ranked, and repairable through audit and remediation flows
